newsitem.title: USA: TFM takes control of Mexico Northeast railroad.
newsitem.headline: TFM takes control of Mexico Northeast railroad.

text.p: Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana said Monday it had assumed control of Mexico's Northeast rail concession, a strategic link on the trade route for the North American Free Trade Agreement.

"We assume management of a railroad which, simply by definition of its location, without any of our planned substantial improvements in marketing, service, equipment and technology, presently transports over 40 percent of Mexico's rail cargo on 19 percent of Mexico's rail track," said TFM chief executive Mario Mohar in a company statement.

TFM said it has put in place $807 million of equity capital and raised $725 million of debt financing, including $325 million of bank debt and $400 million of high yield securities, for the project. It has also established $150 million in bank revolving lines of credit.

TFM, a joint venture of Transportacion Maritima Mexicana and Kansas City Southern Industries Inc, said its purchase of the Northeast line is the largest leveraged acquisition to date in Latin America.
The Mexican government holds a limited voting rights ownership interest in the venture.

The Northeast line serves Mexico City, Monterrey and three of Mexico's four most important ports. It connects them in Laredo, Texas, to Union Pacific Corp and the Texas-Mexican Railroad, which link to other U.S. carriers serving cities throughout the United States.
